zh.principle:
**定理**：P vs NP（P vs NP）。### P 与 NP

P 是确定型图灵机在多项式时间内可判定的语言类；NP 是存在多项式长度证书、且证书可在多项式时间内验证的语言类。判定问题问“是否存在解”，搜索问题问“给出一个解”。对 NP 语言，搜索可以逐位构造证书，但每次判定仍要调用 NP 判定器。### NP-完全与归约

Cook 与 Levin 证明布尔可满足性 SAT 是 NP-完全的：任何 NP 语言 L 都可多项式归约到 SAT，x∈L 当且仅当归约后的公式可满足。Karp 随后给出 21 个 NP-完全问题。归约把“一个问题的多项式算法”传播为“整类问题的多项式算法”。### 为什么尚未解决

P=NP 或 P≠NP 都未被证明。已知证明技术有壁垒：相对化证明无法区分有 oracle 与无 oracle 的世界；自然证明若足够“构造性”和“大规模”，会打破伪随机函数；代数化扩展了相对化，仍不足以解决 P vs NP。
zh.why:
P vs NP 问的是“验证容易是否蕴含求解容易”。如果 P=NP，则 SAT、旅行商、许多优化与搜索问题都有统一的多项式算法，密码学依赖的许多 worst-case 难题会崩塌。### 与密码学的关系

密码学需要的不是“存在一个难实例”，而是“随机实例难”。P≠NP 只排除 worst-case 容易，不能保证 average-case 难。单向函数、伪随机生成器和格假设都比 P≠NP 更强、更具体。### 对方案设计的含义

安全性证明不能写“因为 P≠NP”。必须归约到具体假设，并给出成功概率、查询次数与参数关系；同时要避免把 worst-case 硬度误当成 average-case 安全。
zh.used:
1.复杂度分类：P、NP、NP-完全、coNP、PSPACE 等构成层次；P vs NP 是最近的分界。2.归约工具箱：把新问题归约到 SAT/3-SAT/团/旅行商，判断其难度上界。3.密码参数评估：把攻击归约到已知难题，估计所需密钥长度与敌手优势。4.证明壁垒：在设计新证明前，先检查相对化、自然证明与代数化是否适用。5.教学设计：SAT 是讲解证书、归约与非确定性最标准的例子。### 不能怎么用

不能用 P vs NP 的未决状态给具体协议背书；也不能因为一个问题 NP-完全就断言所有实例都难。
zh.broken:
1.“NP 难”不等于“平均难”：NP-完全问题可能有大量容易实例。2.“P≠NP”不等于“单向函数存在”：需要 average-case 假设与归约。3.“SAT 可满足”不等于“能快速找到解”：判定与搜索不同。4.“归约”不等于“实际算法”：多项式归约可能带巨大常数，工程上不可用。5.“量子算法”不自动解决 P vs NP：Shor 解决的是特定代数问题，不是 SAT。### 证明壁垒

相对化（Baker–Gill–Solovay）说明任何只用 oracle 相对化技术的证明无法分开 P 与 NP；自然证明（Razborov–Rudich）说明一大类组合下界证明会与伪随机函数假设冲突；代数化（Aaronson–Wigderson）覆盖更多代数技术，但仍不够。壁垒不是“不可能”，而是“现有技术不够”。
zh.history:
Cook 在 1971 年证明 SAT 的 NP-完全性，Levin 在 1973 年独立得到类似结果，Karp 在 1972 年列出 21 个 NP-完全问题。此后 P vs NP 成为复杂性理论的核心开放问题，也是 Clay 千禧年问题之一。### 壁垒的发现

Baker、Gill 与 Solovay 在 1975 年给出相对化壁垒；Razborov 与 Rudich 在 1994/1997 年提出自然证明；Aaronson 与 Wigderson 在 2008 年提出代数化。这些结果改变了人们对“如何证明 P≠NP”的预期。

en.principle:
**Theorem**: P vs NP (P vs NP). ### P and NP

P is the class of languages decidable by a deterministic Turing machine in polynomial time; NP is the class of languages with a polynomial-length witness that can be verified in polynomial time. A decision problem asks “does a solution exist”; a search problem asks “give me one”. For an NP language, a witness can be built bit by bit, but each step still calls the NP decider. ### NP-completeness and reductions

Cook and Levin proved that Boolean satisfiability (SAT) is NP-complete: every NP language L reduces in polynomial time to SAT, with x∈L iff the reduced formula is satisfiable. Karp then listed 21 NP-complete problems. A reduction propagates “a polynomial algorithm for one problem” into “a polynomial algorithm for the whole class”. ### Why it is open

Neither P=NP nor P≠NP has been proved. Known techniques face barriers: relativising proofs cannot distinguish worlds with and without an oracle; natural proofs, if sufficiently constructive and large, would break pseudorandom functions; algebrisation extends relativisation but still does not settle P versus NP.
en.why:
P versus NP asks whether easy verification implies easy solving. If P=NP, SAT, travelling salesman and many optimisation and search problems would have a unified polynomial algorithm, and many worst-case problems behind cryptography would collapse.

Cryptography needs random instances to be hard, not merely one hard instance. P≠NP only rules out worst-case easiness; it does not guarantee average-case hardness. One-way functions, pseudorandom generators and lattice assumptions are stronger and more specific than P≠NP.

A security proof cannot say “because P≠NP”. It must reduce to a concrete assumption and state success probability, query counts and parameter relations; it must also avoid mistaking worst-case hardness for average-case security.
en.used:
1. Complexity classification: P, NP, NP-complete, coNP and PSPACE form a hierarchy; P versus NP is the nearest separation. 2. Reduction toolbox: reduce a new problem to SAT/3-SAT/clique/TSP to bound its difficulty. 3. Cryptographic parameter assessment: reduce attacks to known hard problems and estimate key length and adversary advantage. 4. Proof barriers: before designing a new proof, check whether relativisation, natural proofs or algebrisation applies. 5. Teaching: SAT is the standard example of witnesses, reductions and nondeterminism.

The open status of P versus NP cannot endorse a concrete protocol; nor does NP-completeness imply that all instances are hard.
en.broken:
1. “NP-hard” is not “average-case hard”: an NP-complete problem can have many easy instances. 2. “P≠NP” is not “one-way functions exist”: average-case assumptions and reductions are needed. 3. “SAT is satisfiable” is not “a solution can be found quickly”: decision differs from search. 4. “A reduction” is not “a practical algorithm”: a polynomial reduction may have enormous constants. 5. “A quantum algorithm” does not automatically settle P versus NP: Shor solves specific algebraic problems, not SAT.

Relativisation (Baker–Gill–Solovay) says any proof using only oracle-relativising techniques cannot separate P and NP; natural proofs (Razborov–Rudich) say a broad class of combinatorial lower-bound proofs conflicts with pseudorandom-function assumptions; algebrisation (Aaronson–Wigderson) covers more algebraic techniques but still falls short. A barrier is not “impossible”, only “current techniques are insufficient”.
en.history:
Cook proved SAT NP-complete in 1971, Levin independently obtained a similar result in 1973, and Karp listed 21 NP-complete problems in 1972. P versus NP then became a central open problem in complexity theory and a Clay Millennium Problem.

Baker, Gill and Solovay described the relativisation barrier in 1975; Razborov and Rudich proposed natural proofs in 1994/1997; Aaronson and Wigderson proposed algebrisation in 2008. These results changed expectations about how a proof of P≠NP could work.
